npc.old_smuggler.flavor_text: Tried a door like that once. It cost me a hand and a good ship. Bring something worth the risk and we'll talk.
npc.wolf_barkeep.flavor_text: The lights are low and the patrons don't ask questions. A scratched sign above the bar reads NO MILITIA. The operator sizes you up.
step.bar_q1_oldhand.completion_flavor: Word has gone to Barnard's Star. The old man wants to see what you pulled out of that intercept before he decides anything. Give him time.
step.bar_q1_oldhand.description: The Barkeep names an old smuggler who worked a door made of the same material, thirty years ago. The discharge took his hand and the Militia buried the job. He is retired on Barnard's Star b with a story no one believes, and the Militia has watched the old routes since the Incident.
step.bar_q1_oldhand.dialogue.barkeep.int: The old hand knows that door. Thirty years back he was crew on a job at the site - they matched voltage to cycle it, slow work, and the discharge took his hand at the clamp. The Militia buried the whole job; their file says the hardware never existed. He owes me, so I'll send word. He'll want to hear about this signal you intercepted.
step.bar_q1_oldhand.ready_message: The old man will see you, for a price. Come through the bar first: I have a crate that proves you can move cargo the patrols want to find. Run it to Barnard's Star b.
step.bar_q1_oldhand.title: The Old Hand
step.bar_q2_proof.completion_flavor: You hand over the crate, and the old man finally talks. Thirty years come out in one sitting: the job at the door, the matched voltage, the clamp, the Militia file that says none of it happened. When the crew scattered, they cached their hardware in the caves up the ridge - the cell has sat in that dig for thirty years. The ridge is still flown by Militia patrols. He'll contact you when the way is clear.
step.bar_q2_proof.description: The old smuggler deals in proof, not introductions. Collect the crate of unregistered arms from the Barkeep on Earth, then run it to Barnard's Star b. Every Militia patrol on the route can scan it, and every scan is a reason to stop you.
step.bar_q2_proof.dialogue.barkeep.activ: The crate's in your hold. Get it to Barnard's Star b before a patrol scans it.
step.bar_q2_proof.dialogue.barkeep.intro: The old man doesn't take meetings. He takes deliveries. One crate of unregistered arms - if you can walk that past the patrols, you can carry what he gives you next. Get it to Barnard's Star b.
You have the crate. Hand it over, and we'll talk.
You moved the crate clean. The dig is up the ridge, past the old markers. The cell has been down there thirty years and it will still hold a charge - that is the part that should worry you.

The bar sent word, and you come carrying their crate. Then listen. Thirty years ago I worked a job at that door. It was dead metal then - we matched voltage to cycle it, slow work on a quiet circuit. It discharged the frame while my hand was on the clamp. The Militia buried the job, and the cell in their records never existed. Then your intercept hit, and the readings at Mars came back different. The door is drawing power. It is receiving something, and it is humming. A humming door has a live lock, and a live lock can be overloaded. The cell from the old job is still in the dig. Bring it up and I'll tell you the rest.
step.bar_q2_proof.ready_message: The patrol rotation has swung off the ridge. The old man has marked the old crew's cache in the caves. Meet him at the settlement on Barnard's Star b.
step.bar_q2_proof.title: The Proof Run
step.bar_q3_rigparts.completion_flavor: The cell is out of the dig and heavier than it looks. Old Militia hardware, still holding charge. There is exactly one rig off the books that can push current back into it: the listening post at Wolf 359.
step.bar_q3_rigparts.description: The old man has marked the old crew's cache in the Barnard's Star b caves. Descend and recover the rig's power cell - decades-old Militia hardware with the serial ground off. The Militia still flies the ridge.
step.bar_q3_rigparts.dialogue.old_smuggl: The dig is up the ridge, past the old markers. The cell is down in the dark - Militia issue, serial ground off, thirty years on a charge that hasn't decayed. Watch the sky on the way down. The patrols have been thick since your intercept.
step.bar_q3_rigparts.title: The Power Cell
step.bar_q4_blackmarket.completion_flavo: The operator locks the cell into the charger. Filling it takes days; he reads the meter himself and lets nobody else near the rig. He will disconnect it personally when it is full, and he has one warning saved for you about the run home.
step.bar_q4_blackmarket.description: The cell is in your hold - unregistered, unstable, and readable by any scanner that cares to look. Take it to the Wolf 359 listening post. The operator there runs the only off-the-books charger that can fill it.
step.bar_q4_blackmarket.dialogue.old_smu: A patrol took the cell? It was never going to travel quietly. I kept one spare casing from the old job. I can replace it once; after that, the route has to stay yours. Get it to Wolf 359.
step.bar_q4_blackmarket.dialogue.wolf_ba: The cell is on the charger. It is pulling more current than the frame is rated for. Give me time.
The cell is ready. I have warned the Earth Barkeep, and I have not warned the Militia. That is the difference between a delivery and a mistake. Watch the patrols.

That is the cell from the Barnard's job. Militia issue, before they ground the serial. I can charge it - the post draws straight off a reactor tap. What the meter does while it fills is my problem, not yours. Leave it and come back.
step.bar_q4_blackmarket.ready_message: The cell is charged. Collect it at the Wolf 359 post and keep it out of every scanner's line on the way back. The moment you enter Sol, the patrols will read its discharge profile and know exactly what you are carrying.
step.bar_q4_blackmarket.title: Black-Market Recharge
step.bar_q5_charged.completion_flavor: The cell is back on Earth. The rig can be assembled now.
step.bar_q5_charged.description: The charged cell is at the Wolf 359 bar. Collect it and run it to the Barkeep on Earth. A full deep cell has a discharge profile the Militia has on file - the moment you enter Sol, the scanners know what you are carrying.
step.bar_q5_charged.dialogue.barkeep.act: The cell is here. Hand it over and we'll wire the frame.
step.bar_q5_charged.dialogue.barkeep.int: You made it back. Give me the cell before a patrol reads it through the hull. The frame has been behind my bar for thirty years - the old crew's clamps and leads. Rebuilt, it empties the whole cell into the feed in one shot. Bring the cell and we finish this.
step.bar_q5_charged.dialogue.wolf_barkee: The cell is in your hold. Run it to Earth before a patrol decides the discharge profile is reason enough to take you apart.
There it is. Full charge, and a discharge profile the Militia thought they had deleted from the files. Take it to Earth. Every patrol in Sol will read you the moment you jump in.
step.bar_q5_charged.title: The Return Run
step.bar_q6_rig.description: Return to the Barkeep on Earth. The frame is rebuilt: the old crew's clamps and leads, rewired to empty the whole cell into the door's feed in one shot. Thirty years ago the discharge took a hand at the clamp. Nobody holds the clamp this time.
step.bar_q6_rig.dialogue.barkeep.intro: The old frame, rebuilt. Thirty years ago they matched voltage and cycled it slow, and the discharge took his hand at the clamp. This one doesn't cycle. It dead-shorts the feed and empties the whole cell in one shot - the lock trips open or the seal burns, and either way that door is finished holding shut. Welcome to the family, friend.
step.bar_q6_rig.title: The Rig
